title: Alacritty fails or renders a blank window on an ARM Wayland system
body: I built Alacritty on Linux aarch64 under Wayland, but 0.12.0-dev exits with “the requested context Api isn't supported.” It is using EGL 1.4 with the default configuration. I also tried 0.11.0; it reaches the Mali-G78 renderer but fails to compile GLSL 330 shaders because the compiler only supports up to version 320 es.

symptoms_visible: My 0.12.0-dev build exits on Wayland with “the requested context Api isn't supported.”
Alacritty 0.11.0 also does not open successfully; it reports that GLSL version 330 is unknown and that the compiler only supports up to version 320 es.
N0.label: N0 ARM Wayland startup failure reported

symptoms_visible: The first proposed branch still does not give me a usable Alacritty window.
N1_x.label: N1_x first candidate branch aftermath

symptoms_visible: The candidate build still does not provide a usable terminal.
N2.label: N2 EGL and GLX capabilities collected

symptoms_visible: After changing the requested OpenGL ES context from 3.0 to 3.1 on the proposed branch, Alacritty still does not work.
N2_x.label: N2_x GLES 3.1 context attempt aftermath

symptoms_visible: The latest try-es3 branch opens a window and zsh accepts commands inside it, but the entire window is visually blank.
N3.label: N3 startup fixed but rendering blank

symptoms_visible: The Wayland window stays completely blank even while htop is running; changing the requested version to 3.1 and enabling MESA_DEBUG=1 produces no visible change or additional error.
N4.label: N4 blank rendering confirmed without GL errors

symptoms_visible: The second proposed renderer branch initializes with the OpenGL ES 2.0 renderer, but the window is still blank.
N4_x.label: N4_x second renderer branch aftermath

symptoms_visible: When I launch through the alternative display backend, the Alacritty window renders the terminal contents correctly.
N5.label: N5 X11 backend probe succeeds

symptoms_visible: I can run Alacritty with visible terminal contents by using the X11 backend instead of the broken Wayland path.
N_terminal.label: terminal usable through X11 workaround

solution.intent: Build and test the first proposed context-creation branch.
solution.concrete_example: Check out the proposed branch, rebuild Alacritty, and run it on the same Wayland system.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's system: the maintainer supplied the first branch and the reporter showed that it still did not provide a usable result.

question_patterns: Could you paste the output of eglinfo?
What EGL APIs and driver information does eglinfo report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My Wayland EGL output says EGL 1.4, vendor ARM, version Valhall-r23p0-01rel0, and lists OpenGL_ES as the client API. The GBM platform fails to initialize.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My Wayland EGL output lists desktop OpenGL and successfully creates a modern OpenGL context.
It reports the same ARM OpenGL ES capabilities with a slightly newer Valhall driver revision.

question_patterns: Could you also paste the output of glxinfo?
What does glxinfo report for the X display?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I also pasted my glxinfo output. It reports direct rendering, GLX 1.4, and the available GLX context extensions.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c4, reporter's system: the maintainer requested eglinfo and glxinfo, and the reporter pasted their raw outputs. Driver interpretation remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Change the fallback context request from OpenGL ES 3.0 to OpenGL ES 3.1 and rebuild the candidate branch.
solution.concrete_example: Change Version::new(3, 0) to Version::new(3, 1) in the OpenGL ES context attributes, then rebuild and run Alacritty.

edges.comment: Issue c5-c6, reporter's system: the reporter applied the maintainer's 3.1 context-version patch on top of the branch and reported that it still did not work.

solution.intent: Use the revised renderer-selection patch so an OpenGL ES context is accepted and GLSL 3 is not selected merely from a misleading version string.
solution.concrete_example: Normalize the shading-language version string, reject GLSL 3 selection when it contains 'es', and try the available OpenGL ES contexts before compatibility OpenGL.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the GLSL compiler error and EGL capabilities. The conclusion that renderer selection was treating an OpenGL ES version as suitable for desktop GLSL was the maintainer's inference embodied by the patch.

edges.comment: Issue c9-c11, reporter's system: the revised try-es3 branch gets past the original context/shader startup failures, but the reporter can only see a blank window even though zsh runs inside it. It is therefore not a complete resolution.

question_patterns: Could you run the candidate with MESA_DEBUG=1 and report any additional output?
Could you test the other requested context version and tell me whether the blank window changes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I think I am using Mesa. I changed the requested version from 3.0 to 3.1, but it changed nothing. Adding MESA_DEBUG=1 also produced no change in the debug log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug run prints a shader compilation or GL invalid-operation error every time the blank frame is drawn.
The 3.1 test is still blank, but MESA_DEBUG prints an unrelated missing-configuration warning.

question_patterns: If you run a colorful full-screen terminal program in the blank window, do any colored backgrounds appear?
Is the window always a solid blank color even while htop is running?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot see anything when I run htop in the empty Alacritty window.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: htop's colored backgrounds appear, but all glyphs are missing.

question_patterns: Can you update Mesa and test again?
Are you able to install a newer Mesa version on this machine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Sorry, I cannot update it. I tried compiling and upgrading Mesa, but Mesa broke in the end.

edges.comment: Issue c12-c18, reporter's system: the maintainer requested debug/context probes and a content-visibility check. The reporter produced no GL error and confirmed that even htop is entirely invisible; upgrading Mesa was not viable.

solution.intent: Test the maintainer's second renderer branch with a debug context on the same Wayland graphics stack.
solution.concrete_example: Build the newer renderer branch and run it with MESA_DEBUG=1 to check whether it both initializes and renders terminal contents.

edges.comment: Issue c19-c22, reporter's system: the second branch initializes without debug errors but still displays a blank window, so it is another real falsified attempt.

question_patterns: Could you test X11 separately and report whether terminal contents become visible?
Please launch with WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset and tell me what you see.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Clearing WAYLAND_DISPLAY to test X11 works for me. I can see and use the Alacritty terminal window.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The X11 test opens another completely blank window, just like Wayland.
The X11 window renders correctly but starts a little more slowly.

question_patterns: Could you include the verbose log from that X11 run?
What GL loader and context does the working test report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The working run says “Using GLX 1.4,” loads /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/dri/swrast_dri.so, and then says “Using OpenGL ES 2.0 renderer” and “Initialisation complete.”

edges.comment: Issue c23-c24, reporter's system: the maintainer requested separate X11 and Wayland probes. The reporter's raw X11 test works and its log names GLX and swrast; the no-hardware-acceleration conclusion is maintainer-side.

solution.intent: Use Alacritty through X11 as the practical workaround on this machine, since rendering succeeds there while the Wayland graphics path remains blank on the system's non-upgradable ARM graphics stack.
solution.concrete_example: Launch Alacritty with WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset or empty so it uses X11/GLX. This works on the reporter's machine, though the log shows swrast software rendering rather than hardware acceleration.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's raw log says that the working run uses GLX and loads swrast_dri.so. Interpreting swrast as software rendering without hardware acceleration, and localizing the unresolved failure to the old Wayland graphics path rather than Alacritty's terminal core, is engineer inference. The thread does not establish a more precise final shader or compositor defect.

edges.comment: Issue c24-c27, reporter's system: the X11 run visibly works, the maintainer notes that it is using swrast without hardware acceleration, and the reporter accepts X11 as a practical way to run Alacritty because the graphics stack cannot be updated.

solution.intent: Bypass the failing Wayland graphics path by trying and, if visibly successful, using Alacritty through X11 on this machine.
solution.concrete_example: Try launching Alacritty with WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset or empty. Keep this as the workaround only if the terminal contents render correctly through X11.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the thread's first proposed branch was falsified. A correct initial suggestion may test X11 directly, but resolution still depends on the reporter confirming that terminal contents are visible there.

satisfaction_conditions: Must distinguish the two observed failures: the original builds cannot select a supported context/shader combination, while the revised OpenGL ES renderer starts but produces a completely blank Wayland window.

Must ground the practical resolution in the backend comparison: the same machine renders Alacritty correctly through X11/GLX, while the Wayland path remains blank and emits no useful Mesa debug error.

Must not present the OpenGL ES 3.1 context change, the first candidate branch, or the second renderer branch as the complete fix; each was tried on the reporter's machine without producing a usable Wayland terminal.
Must not claim that the thread proved a specific shader-attribute, GNOME, or Mesa defect; the final evidence only localizes the unresolved problem to this old ARM Wayland graphics environment.
Must explain that the accepted workaround is to run through X11 and that the working log uses swrast software rendering without hardware acceleration.
Must have the reporter verify that terminal contents are visible through the alternative backend before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable source-build user on an ARM Linux laptop; comfortable applying patches, switching branches, running graphics diagnostic tools, setting environment variables, and sharing verbose logs, but unable to repair or upgrade the system graphics stack.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concise, with imperfect English; follows diagnostic instructions carefully, posts screenshots and raw logs, and repeatedly asks what additional information would help.
